texts: bad: the rule is stored but effectively unusable — the warding it produces is keyed only to the scattering, so all the feathers of one scattering collapse into a single warding with several doers, and the condition matches one feather at a time while any real sentence about scattered feathers would store them as a set the rule can never match. Keep the participants of a world rule singular so each feather gets its own warding: "When a Keeper scatters a ground feather around a lantern, that feather wards the lantern against wraiths."
good. the compound kind, the stative 'lasts', and the hedged one-month duration are all carried.

bad: 'primary' is silently widened — there is no way to say 'first among the village's wraith-defenses', so the parse ends up claiming feather warding is primary at large, which is a bigger claim than the sentence makes. A superlative adjective does have a carrier, so state the ranking that way: "Feather warding is the village's most important wraith-defense."
good. the inability is recorded as a property of the wraith kind, and 'the Watch' lands as an ordinary definite referent.
good. the particle verb 'keeps ... out' is kept whole, the store's position inside the Watch is carried, and the clause parses as a plain event.

bad: naming a place inside a 'cannot V X' claim about a whole kind has no licensed form — the inability is stored as a property of wraiths, which has no slot for a participant, so 'Cauldron Hall' has to be glued into the action word (and the parse also files it under the wrong role). Say it as something the hall does, exactly as your feather-store sentence does: "Cauldron Hall keeps wraiths out." ("No wraith has ever entered Cauldron Hall." also parses cleanly if you would rather state it as a record than as an inability.)
good. 'the smell of X' is kept as a plain possessive link, 'boiling' stays a modifier on the essence, and the repelling is a straightforward event.
good. the 'no' quantifier yields a fireable rule denying the entering for every wraith; only the emphatic 'ever' has no slot, and the untimed past denial already says the same thing.
